items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: last night I went down and did a set with Terry Gibbs and Buddy DeFranco down at the other hotel.

ctx.x: Yeah. I enjoy it very much. I love working with my band, but I love working with a lot of other bands, as you just mentioned, this weekend is pretty busy with me. And tomorrow I’m going to be down at the Marriott where there’s another jazz party going on with Terry Gibbs Dream Band. And then tonight I’m going up to Santa Barbara to do a

concert with Supersax. Now Med Flory has added a brass section to Supersax, and four voices. So it’s now the L.A. Voices he calls it. Sue Raney is the lead singer and the brass section, so it’s kind of, what do you call it, Supersax with voices? Or, I don’t know, it doesn’t matter what it’s called, it’s still big band and it’s fun to do. I like all kinds of playing. I enjoy doing what we’re doing here at this and I’m playing, I just finished, as I said, last night I went down and did a set with Terry Gibbs and…
You’ve got to change hats from one day to the next.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: But there’s guys that have been working for me for thirty years now, when I put the band together. And so every once in a while, that cliché, when they make me an offer I can’t refuse. But now they’re all leaders by the way. Med Flory, Frank Capp.

ctx.x: And colleges are buying them left and right. I was just doing a clinic and a few of the college people said, “Are you kidding, we ordered fourteen.” Because they don’t write arrangements like that anymore. They’re just straight ahead swing music. And especially if you want to show the band off, if you play the arrangements like it’s really written, because I actually patterned the band after the Benny Goodman band because Benny played in and out. Because it didn’t blend with the section. It did, but it would…

better, he still forgot to turn the page over, so he came in again, and I have to play after that, the vibes play. Then comes the clarinet. So he’s picking up the clarinet and he’s playing all alone while I’m playing my solo. Then he realizes what he’s doing. Once again the audience fell out, and you know what? That was the standard thing through the whole hour and a half we do. I’d asked Med, “Med, you want to sing?” “Anything you want, Terry.” And Med’s very funny. All the guys. You know I play straight man for…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I took Frank Capp on drums, my drummer, and Paul Smith who was doing my TV shows.

ctx.x: Well I’ll tell you how it all started. I used to be — Steve Allen was my friend. I was friends with Steve in the early 40s, late 40s. He became my friend then he became a big fan of mine, you know. And when he got his TV show he got me as a guest all the time, I was a guest a lot. And we were doing the show in California and I did his show with them and one of the producers, he loved me. He loved my dumb sense of humor, because I’m not a comedian but I’ve got the wit sort of like Steve’s. Steve loved me because,…

they said, “Okay we want you, it’s your job, but Steve Allen had a nine piece orchestra, we’ll give you a nine piece orchestra.” I said, “I don’t want it.” They said, “Well what do you mean?” I said, “You mean they give me a big band because we’re opposite Johnny Carson? Or opposite Elliot Lawrence who was with Les Crane — those shows at that time they all had 16 piece bands. And to me a 16 piece band — give me a sextet. I said sextet? Can you make it with a sextet? You see working with Steve Allen, of course I…

in at Letter D, the ending.” Play the intro — the singer never knew we never played the middle. We’d never do it. So that’s what I learned. So I did that for my TV shows, and then, you know it was, it just came naturally to me because the harder part got later on. See all the talent we had for the first maybe two or three weeks, and that’s why Regis, in last, where all the talent that already were booked for Steve Allen. And Steve was a big jazz fan so he’d have Sarah Vaughan, Stan Getz, Oscar Peterson, Count…
